main.result_summary:
The 2001-10-21 consolidation is committed as `590e69c1`. Lint and `sleep-audit.py` were both green before the commit. I did not push: your instructions say both "do not push, the runner pushes" and "git push origin main", and I followed the more specific one, so the runner still has to push. The week had 83 messages with notes. 76 are now cited in memory and 7 are listed as drops in `dataset/drops/sleep-103.tsv` (two repeats, one social note, one phone number, one with no owner action, two where the owner was only copied). The main new facts:
- The owner cancelled his San Francisco conference panel and Zimin Lu went in his place.
- He joined Carnegie Mellon's MSCF Advisory Board; the first meeting is 12 Dec in New York.
- He confirmed the Georgia Tech talk for 1 Nov.
- He told a candidate he only hires to replace people who leave.
- Frank Wolak of Stanford warned against Enron backing PJM-style nodal pricing, and Martin Lin replied.
- The Argentina model is moving to SDDP, and Tom Halliburton leaves Enron on 2 Nov.
- Enron moved HR to report to the Office of the Chairman and announced the 22 Oct managing directors' meeting and the 23 Oct all-employee meeting.

I opened two new topic files: one for the owner's weekly newsletter column (including his 21 Oct "Market for Lemons" piece) and one for the energy book Wiley is chasing. Luke Eleftheriou, Praveen Kumar and Joannie Williamson reached five messages this week, so they now have person files and alias-table entries. To keep growth within the audit's limits, I moved each over-target file's oldest lines word for word into `memory/archive/<domain>/2001/` and shortened seven long lists of links to the archive. The domain indexes and `state.md` are refreshed and the inbox is archived. There were no sleep-task or feedback blocks, no questions were due for closing, nothing new went to `questions.md`, and the Rick Bryant alias approval is still open.
